content: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of istradefylline through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. In clinical trials, istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cobicistat and itraconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Itraconazole and darunavir also increase each other's effects through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. When co-administering itraconazole with darunavir/ritonavir, itraconazole should not exceed 200 mg/day. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cobicistat and ketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when co-administered with cobicistat. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. As a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Letermovir increases the levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. Cobicistat and levoketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when co-administered with cobicistat. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Darunavir increases the levels of lidocaine by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. Darunavir decreases the effects of linagliptin through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Darunavir decreases the effects of liraglutide through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Concomitant use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase lofexidine plasma levels. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Darunavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
